children: Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL, Financials), the parent company of Google and one of the largest cloud and AI providers, is taking its infrastructure deeper into university research.
Google Public Sector is partnering with Morgan State University to build an AI-focused research campus supporting work in cybersecurity, climate science, health science and large language models.
The project will give researchers access to high-end GPU computing through Google Cloud and Nvidia infrastructure.
That is the obvious part. The longer-term opportunity is what happens after students and researchers become comfortable building on Google's technology.

Morgan State also plans to create a Google-focused Center of Excellence for AI skills and workforce training. Faculty will gain access to Google for Startups, while the university will use Google SecOps and Mandiant security tools for research requiring stricter controls.

The partnership also connects Google to Morgan State's Obsidian AI platform, including projects involving traffic and urban mobility in Baltimore. For Alphabet, these deals are small compared with multibillion-dollar cloud contracts.
But they can still matter. Training future engineers and researchers on Google Cloud can make the platform harder to replace later.
For investors, the question is whether partnerships like this can quietly translate into greater cloud adoption as universities, startups and public-sector organizations expand their AI spending.

title: Google Just Made an AI Move That Could Matter Far More Than Wall Street Thinks
